# X Finally Lets Parents Put Limits on Their Teens' App Activity

## Parents can now set daily time limits, approve new followers, decide who can send DMs, and more. They can't, however, read messages exchanged in a thread.
...
X, formerly Twitter, has finally rolled out parental controls to help guardians supervise accounts of teens aged 13 to 17.

Users under 18 already have restricted accounts by default, with only approved followers able to view their posts and accounts they follow able to send them DMs. The new parental controls go one step further, allowing parents to set daily time limits, require teens to get approval for new followers, restrict their For You feeds to content posted by accounts they follow, disable specific words and sensitive content, and gatekeep accounts they can chat with.

However, this doesn’t mean teens lose their privacy. Parents will still not be able to check their messages, searches, or posts they’ve already seen. Parents can’t create posts, reply, like, or send messages on their behalf, nor can they sign in to a teen’s account and change its password.

More importantly, both sides must agree to begin supervision. Once placed under supervision, teens can request to end it at any time. The right to approve or deny that request lies with the parent or guardian.

“Supervision on X starts with a handshake and ends automatically when a teen becomes an adult. Parents get guardrails, not a window into their teen's private life,” said Mridul Singhai, X’s product engineering lead.

A guardian can supervise up to five teen accounts, while a teen can be linked only to one guardian account at a time. To begin linking, parents should go to Settings and privacy > Security and access > Parental Controls > Get Started.

seltz.title: Is X (Twitter) Safe for Teens? What Parents Should Know (2026)
seltz.snippet:
There is one fact about X that matters more than every other piece of safety advice combined, and most parents don't know it: **X is the only major social platform that formally permits pornography.**

Instagram bans it. TikTok bans it. YouTube bans it. Facebook bans it. On 3 June 2024, X went the other way — replacing its old Sensitive Media rules with an **Adult Content policy** that explicitly allows users to post consensual pornography, on the grounds that \"sexual expression, whether visual or written, can be a legitimate form of artistic expression.\"

The minimum age for an X account is 13.

## How Much Adult Content Is Actually There?

Reuters reported an internal Twitter estimate that **13% of all content on the platform was adult content** — and that was in 2022, before the policy was formalised and before the well-documented growth in porn bot accounts.

So this isn't a moderation failure of the kind every platform has. On Instagram, pornography is against the rules and gets removed when found. On X, it's permitted content that the platform has decided to host. That's a different thing, and it deserves a different response from parents.

## What X's Protections Actually Are

X does place restrictions around it, and they're worth stating accurately:

- Adult content must be **labelled** and sits behind a content warning users have to click through.
- It's **not permitted in highly visible places** — profile pictures, banners, headers.
- Users **under 18, or without a birth date on their profile, cannot view it**.
- Content sexualising minors, or depicting non-consent or exploitation, is prohibited outright.
- The policy covers AI-generated material too — including cartoons, hentai and anime.

Now the part that matters. **The age gate is a birth date the user typed in themselves.**

A thirteen-year-old who wants to see adult content changes one number in their profile.

## Parents can now set daily time limits, approve new followers, decide who can send DMs, and more. They can't, however, read messages exchanged in a thread.
...
X, formerly Twitter, has finally rolled out parental controls to help guardians supervise accounts of teens aged 13 to 17.

Users under 18 already have restricted accounts by default, with only approved followers able to view their posts and accounts they follow able to send them DMs. The new parental controls go one step further, allowing parents to set daily time limits, require teens to get approval for new followers, restrict their For You feeds to content posted by accounts they follow, disable specific words and sensitive content, and gatekeep accounts they can chat with.

However, this doesn’t mean teens lose their privacy. Parents will still not be able to check their messages, searches, or posts they’ve already seen. Parents can’t create posts, reply, like, or send messages on their behalf, nor can they sign in to a teen’s account and change its password.

More importantly, both sides must agree to begin supervision. Once placed under supervision, teens can request to end it at any time. The right to approve or deny that request lies with the parent or guardian.
